Validate presence of required columns

Source: R/validation.R
validate_schema.Rd

Check whether a data.frame contains all the columns required for subsequent processing.

Usage

validate_schema(dataframe, required_columns, boolean_form = FALSE)

Arguments

dataframe

The data.frame to check.

required_columns

A character vector with the names of the required columns.

boolean_form

Logical (TRUE/FALSE). If TRUE, returns a simple boolean. If FALSE, returns a detailed message.

Value

  • If boolean_form = TRUE: A boolean.

  • If boolean_form = FALSE: A character string (success or error message).

Details

The function supports two output modes via the boolean_form argument:

  • Boolean mode: Returns TRUE or FALSE. Useful inside if conditions.

  • Verbose mode (default): Returns a text message explicitly listing missing columns, or confirming that all required columns are present.

See also

Other Validation functions: deduplicate_rows(), enforce_types(), read_raw_csv(), standardize_colnames()

Examples

df <- data.frame(id = 1:3, salary = c(100, 200, 300))

# Success case (message)
validate_schema(df, c("id", "salary"))
#> [1] "All required colums are present in the dataframe"

# Failure case (message)
validate_schema(df, c("id", "salary", "age"))
#> [1] "The dataframe in not complete and it's missing age"

# Success case (boolean)
if (validate_schema(df, c("id"), boolean_form = TRUE)) {
  print("All required columns are present.")
}
#> Error in validate_schema(df, c("id"), boolean_form = TRUE): unused argument (boolean_form = TRUE)
